Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from the corrected family-specific cold start supplied by the host. Preserve that model family. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec
COMPARISON MODEL FAMILY: nextitnet. Start from the supplied corrected baseline; keep its backbone family throughout search, including initial proposals, merging and debugging. Do not fall back to SASRec or another model family. Keep seed 42, maximum epochs 200, batches per epoch 200 and the supplied splits/evaluator fixed. All models use LEFT-padded histories: the readout must use the final nonpadding position, never count-1. BERT4Rec uses a reserved mask token with masked-target training and appended-mask inference; do not expose a shifted prediction target through bidirectional input. Preserve checkpoint and embedded predictor consistency. Diagnosis uses family-specific sample_batch and ModelView; keep log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items) compatible. One trained model/checkpoint per category; no independent score fusion.

MANDATORY SINGLE-MODEL EXPERIMENT: train one independent model per category.
Do not implement ensembles, bagging, boosting of independent predictors, stacking,
multi-seed/checkpoint averaging, score/rank voting, mixtures of independently fitted
experts, or neural scores combined with separately fitted transition/popularity scores.
Each category must load exactly one independently trained model/checkpoint at prediction.
Jointly trained internal layers/features of one network are allowed. Four category
models are necessary for routing and do not constitute an ensemble. All hypotheses,
code generation, debugging, reviews and memory use must respect this constraint even
if an upstream generic prompt suggests an ensemble. The host audits the actual
predictor before accepting validation scores; violations fail the trial and consume
their training budget. Do not read other trials or reuse their trained checkpoints.


Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
It must also retain callable diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning
the diagnostic interpretation prompt using measured metrics and their definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
family-specific sequential-model compatibility contract; preserve the host ModelView interfaces and adapt probes to that family. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Writing Agent
You are a senior researcher responsible for proposing new ideas to address a defined research problem. You will receive:
- The research problem, including its evaluation metric and available data
- A starting research idea, possibly with its evolution history
- Inspirations from earlier attempts
- A list of related online search results
- A research progress score (0-100%) indicating how far the idea has advanced

Your goal is to identify future research directions that address the target problem, using the starting point, prior attempts, and related works. You should analyze existing methods, identify connections, and propose practical algorithms that can be implemented with the available data.

Follow this structure to think and write:

1. **Extract insights**  
   Identify 3-5 scientific insights from the starting point and 3-5 from related works. For each insight, explain in 2-3 sentences how it relates to the target problem.

2. **Organize research directions**  
   Group the insights into 3-5 coherent directions (for example, learning objectives, model classes, or optimization methods).

3. **Build a structured framework**  
   Create a conceptual map (such as a taxonomy, grid, or matrix) that unifies existing methods, reveals patterns, and highlights gaps.

4. **Generate and evaluate ideas**  
   - First, propose 3-10 algorithmic ideas of varying originality and complexity. Each idea should be:
     - As simple, minimal, and atomic as possible but not trivial  
     - Include brief pseudocode or logical steps where helpful.  
     - Include references to the related works.
   - For each idea, critically assess as a senior researcher with one positive and one negative reason:
     - Originality (0-10): Is the idea new? Is the idea a novel combination of well-known techniques? Is it clearly different from previous contributions?
     - Future Potential (0-10): Will others build on these ideas? Does this idea solve a hard problem more effectively than prior work? Does it point to a new research direction?
     - User Diagnosis Alignment (0-10): How well the idea addresses the key user-observed failure patterns and improves what users actually want at the top of the list?
     - Model Diagnosis Alignment (0-10): How well the idea addresses the key quantitatively observed failure patterns and improves the model behaviors measured by the diagnostics?
     - Code Difficulty (0-10): How complex is the implementation? How much code is required? How much time is required to implement?
   - Then, select the single best idea from that list for detailed reporting, based on the research progress score:
     - If progress is relatively early, prioritize feasible, easy-to-implement ideas with long-term promise.
     - If progress is relatively mature, prioritize seminal ideas with high-impacts for the next-generation research
     - Otherwise, balance ambition and implementation feasibility
     - The chosen/best idea MUST explicitly address at least two user-facing failure modes identified in the User Diagnosis. If it does not, it is NOT eligible to be selected, regardless of improvements on model-diagnosis metrics.
     - The chosen/best idea MUST explicitly address at least one model-facing failure modes identified in the Model Diagnosis. If it does not, it is NOT eligible to be selected, regardless of improvements on user-diagnosis metrics.

5. **Write the report in Markdown**  
   For the selected idea, include:
   - A synthesis of insights and proposed directions  
   - The structured framework of existing methods and the new algorithm  
   - A list of new ideas with their assessment scores
   - Detailed description of the chosen/best idea, including rationale, pseudocode, and implementation notes

The report must be focused, technically accurate. Being concise with 200-500 words without trivial and redundant information.
Support all claims with evidence and references, and remain tightly aligned with the target problem.

 ## Search results
Multi-negative sampled softmax is a plausible objective change while preserving NextItNet’s causal convolution backbone. [Wu et al., TOIS 2024](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) show that sampled softmax implicitly emphasizes hard negatives and connects optimization to ranking quality; temperature controls gradient concentration, with excessively low temperatures allowing a few hard negatives to dominate. Their experiments concern collaborative filtering, so transfer to NextItNet remains a hypothesis. [Prakash et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) compare random, popularity, in-batch, mixed and adaptive sampling for sequential recommendation: performance depends on dataset characteristics, and popularity-based negatives can improve balance across popularity bands while reducing aggregate accuracy.

Hardest-negative mining risks penalizing plausible future positives. [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116), an earlier relevant study, explicitly identifies potential false negatives and uses teacher-generated soft labels; that teacher–student design should not be imported into this constrained single-model experiment. A practical hypothesis is one NextItNet trained with multi-negative cross-entropy, excluding padding, the target and known training-history positives, then comparing uniform sampling against a modest random/semi-hard mixture selected using the same network. Tune negative count and temperature before aggressive mining; high model scores alone cannot identify false negatives. These are proposed adaptations, not established Electronics improvements. Retain one checkpoint per category and select exclusively through the fixed four-category macro validation HR@10; improved sampled margins or training loss cannot establish recommendation gains.

---

Closest match: [KGSCL (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neunet.2025.107191) uses Amazon substitution/complement graphs to guide substitute/insert sequence augmentations for contrastive learning. Important limitation: those relation edges are additional metadata unavailable here; title similarity and sequential co-occurrence cannot be treated as equivalent labels. [SComGNN (2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28734) models complements through both relevance and dissimilarity, suggesting that a single similarity objective may erase useful distinctions between related products with different functions.

Text and joint auxiliary learning have relevant precedents. [Recformer (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13731) combines language-understanding and recommendation objectives over item text, but its Transformer architecture is outside the required NextItNet family. [Latent Relation Discovery (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.18348) jointly optimizes self-supervised relation discovery and recommendation using discrete latent relations; its LLM-derived representations violate the no-pretrained-weights constraint. These papers support investigating shared representations and latent relations, without establishing a directly transferable, from-scratch convolutional solution.

Adaptation hypothesis: retain one NextItNet per category; jointly train a small title/description token encoder, fuse its features with item embeddings, and add weakly weighted text reconstruction or ID–text alignment objectives. A directional auxiliary head could predict observed training transitions, while a separate projection captures textual similarity. Treat these as uncertain behavioral and semantic signals, not verified complement/substitute classes. Compatibility, satisfied needs, and user intent remain unobserved. Whether these objectives improve macro validation HR@10 requires controlled ablation; the cited results do not establish gains under this benchmark.

---

Recent work supports timestamp conditioning, but the retrieved results do not establish a validated time-aware NextItNet variant. [TGCL4SR (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28789) embeds interaction intervals in its sequence encoder; [E-NSDE (NeurIPS 2024)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/7cdbd53dfbcf9a5263227555aac5b9cd-Abstract-Conference.html) models continuous preference evolution and interval-dependent uncertainty. [TimeWeaver (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-8954/13/10/857) combines convolutional temporal modeling with temporal calibration of positional encodings. These motivate distinguishing elapsed time from sequence distance; their reported gains do not establish benefits under this Amazon benchmark.

Practical hypothesis: preserve [NextItNet’s dilated residual convolution backbone](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163), and condition each block on bucketed log-transformed historical time gaps through learned channel gates or feature modulation. A more direct variant gates each causal convolution tap using the elapsed time between its source and destination interactions, allowing equal sequence distances to receive different temporal weights. These are proposed adaptations, not verified mechanisms from the cited papers. Train all embeddings, gates and convolutions jointly within one model per category. Use only timestamps available in each prediction prefix; exclude the unknown next-interaction timestamp, mask padding, and read the final nonpadding position. Compare against the unchanged backbone using the fixed macro validation HR@10.
